user: what led to the development of the blues?
assistant: The development of the blues is associated with the newly acquired freedom of the slaves. As former slaves became acculturated, their secular and religious music began to reflect their psychological, social, and economic changes, and was linked to the national ideological emphasis on the individual and the popularity of Booker T. Washington's teachings.  The style evolved over a long period and existed in approaching its modern form before the term blues was introduced and before the style was thoroughly documented. Ethnomusicologist Gerhard Kubik traces the roots of many of the elements that were to develop into the blues back to the African continent , the "cradle of the blues.' Many blues elements , such as the call-and-response format , can be traced back to the music of Africa . The use of melisma and a wavy , nasal intonation also suggests a connection between the music of West and Central Africa and the blues. The first appearance of the blues is not well defined and is often dated between 1870 and 1900 , a period that coincides with the emancipation of the slaves and the transition from slavery to sharecropping and small-scale agricultural production in the southern United States. One important early mention of something closely resembling the blues comes from 1901 , when an archaeologist in Mississippi described the songs of black workers which had lyrical themes and technical elements in common with the blues. The launch of the field of race music by record companies like Paramount Records and OKeh Records, which was mostly blues targeted at African American audiences, also contributed to the development of the blues.
user: How did Booker T. Washington's teachings contribute to the development of the blues?
assistant: According to Lawrence Levine , there was a direct relationship between the national ideological emphasis upon the individual, the popularity of Booker T. Washington's teachings , and the rise of the blues. Booker T. Washington's teachings contributed to the development of the blues through their influence on the acculturation of African Americans during the early 1900s. Ethnomusicologist Gerhard Kubik traces the roots of many of the elements that were to develop into the blues back to the African continent , the `` cradle of the blues '' .
user: Are there different kinds of blues?
assistant: Yes, there are different kinds of blues, however, I do not have a whole list of them.   The Great Migration of poor black workers from the South into the industrial cities brought traditional jazz and blues music to the city , resulting in Chicago blues and `` Chicago - style '' Dixieland jazz .  Beginning in the 1920s and accelerating greatly in the 1940s , the blues began rapidly diversifying into a broad spectrum of new styles . These included an uptempo , energetic style called rhythm and blues ( R&B ) , a merger of blues and Anglo - Celtic song called country music and the fusion of hymns and spirituals with blues structures called gospel music . Later than these other styles , in the 1940s , a blues , R&B and country fusion eventually called rock and roll developed. The diversity of blues styles reflects the genre's evolution over time and its ability to adapt to different contexts and influences.
user: Memphis versus Texas blues
assistant: I have no information about Memphis blues and Texas blues.
user: Didn't the blues evolve from the songs of slave field laborers?
assistant: Yes, the origins of the blues can be traced back to the songs of African American slave field laborers. These songs often contained lyrical themes and technical elements similar to those found in the blues. The use of the call-and-response format, melisma, and a wavy, nasal intonation in blues music can all be traced back to African musical traditions. The first appearance of the blues is often dated between 1870 and 1900, during the period when slaves were being emancipated and transitioning to sharecropping and small-scale agricultural production in the southern United States.

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Chicago blues outstanding artists
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
Some outstanding artists in the Chicago blues scene include Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, Junior Wells, Chester Burnett, Edie Boyd,  and both Sonny Boy Williamsons. These musicians were instrumental in shaping the Chicago blues sound, which is characterized by its use of electric instruments and urban rhythms. They also influenced many other musicians and genres, including rock and roll.

[The Start of Document]
Illinois
The Great Migration of poor black workers from the South into the industrial cities brought traditional jazz and blues music to the city , resulting in Chicago blues and `` Chicago - style '' Dixieland jazz . Notable blues artists included Muddy Waters , Junior Wells , Howlin ' Wolf and both Sonny Boy Williamsons ; jazz greats included Nat King Cole , Gene Ammons , Benny Goodman , and Bud Freeman . Chicago is also well known for its soul music .

Great Migration (African American)
The Great Migration had effects on music as well as other cultural subjects . Many Blues singers migrated from Delta - Mississippi to Chicago to escape racial discrimination . Muddy Waters and Chester Burnett are two of the most well - known Blues singers who migrated to Chicago . Great Delta - born pianist Eddie Boyd told Living Blues Magazine , `` I thought of coming to Chicago where I could get away from some of that racism and where I would have an opportunity to , well , do something with my talent ... It was n't peaches and cream ( in Chicago ) , man , but it was a hell of a lot better than down there where I was born . ''

Origins of the blues
The social and economic reasons for the appearance of the blues are not fully known . Blues has evolved from an unaccompanied vocal music of poor black laborers into a wide variety of styles and subgenres , with regional variations across the United States . African American work songs were an important precursor to the modern blues ; these included the songs sung by laborers like stevedores and roustabouts , and the field hollers and `` shouts '' of slaves . The first appearance of the blues is not well defined and is often dated between 1870 and 1900 , a period that coincides with the emancipation of the slaves and the transition from slavery to sharecropping and small - scale agricultural production in the southern United States .
[The End of Document]
